deep.reconstruction:
The page has no mathematical derivation.

(a) Top, upright, in a later Latin hand: 'Similiter causaque, ego ambote, fumant cum de Suis.' This is not grammatical classical Latin. It is probably a macaronic word game or riddle (Latin-looking words meant to be read aloud as another language) or a quotation jotted down. It has no mathematical content.

(b) The rest of the page is written with the book turned 180 degrees, in an older German Kurrent hand. It is a ledger of money lent out from a cash box ('Cassa'). The dates (1794, 1798, 1799) fall in Gauss's student years or before. The hand and context suggest the notebook may have been used by someone else first (for example a family or household account) before Gauss used it from the other end as a memorandum book. That attribution is my inference.

Entries:
1. 25 Sept 1794: 300 Reichsthaler in 'schweres Geld' (full-weight coin) lent on a mortgage bond ('Hypothek-Obligation') to Joh. Diet. Gottl. Oppermann(?), at 3 1/2 percent per year. The implied annual interest, 300*0.035 = 10.5 Rth, is my computation and is not written.
2. 18 Feb 1798: 80 Rth in Conventions-Münze lent to a person whose name is hard to read, on a bond or bill, at 4 percent per year. The implied annual interest is 80*0.04 = 3.2 Rth, again my computation. This entry is cancelled by a large diagonal X, presumably marking repayment.
3. A struck-through line, apparently '1799 ausgeliehen … Rth 20 …', recording a further small loan that was also cancelled.

No calculation, no interest computation and no derivation appears on the page.

results.what: Household loan ledger: principal amounts and simple annual interest rates (300 Rth at 3.5%, 80 Rth at 4%).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a financial or household ledger of loans from 1794–1799, possibly not even in Gauss's hand, plus a Latin-like phrase. It contains no mathematics beyond implied simple interest.

checkable.asserts: Annual interest on 300 Rth at 3 1/2 percent is 10.5 Rth (implied, not written).
Annual interest on 80 Rth at 4 percent is 3.2 Rth (implied, not written).

transcription_corrections: The 1798 entry (from 'Ao 1798 d. 18 Febr.' to 'zu 4 pCt p. Ao.') is cancelled by a large diagonal X across the whole block, not only the last line.
The 1798 debtor's name line (rendered 'an [?]') appears to contain a personal name with initials (something like 'Carl Christ. …'); it is not 'auf Wechsel'. The reading remains uncertain.
The cancelled bottom line begins with the year 1799 (written small at the left) and contains 'Rth 20'. The word after the year appears to be 'ausgeliehen' or a similar word, not a clear reading.
The inverted ledger is in an older Kurrent hand distinct from the Latin hand at the top and is likely not Gauss's own memorandum entry. The dates predate his use of the notebook.
